events.region: Matagorda Bay; Coastal waters from Freeport to Matagorda Ship Channel TX out 20 NM; Coastal waters from High Island to Freeport TX out 20 NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms are currently
moving over Matagorda Bay and the nearshore waters. Some storms
are capable of producing gusty winds, locally higher seas,
lightning strikes, and hail.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms
pass.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Los Olmos Creek Near Falfurrias affecting Brooks County.

.Latest observations show that Low Olmos Creek near Falfurrias has
risen to Action Stage (5.0 feet) with a current level of 6.21 feet.
Levels are expected to remain above Action Stage through tonight and
likely through Wednesday (at least).

For the Los Olmos Creek...including Falfurrias...elevated river
levels are forecast.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Los Olmos Creek near Falfurrias.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding reaches 120 feet wide
into flood plain-persons vulnerable to lowland flooding should move
equipment to higher ground

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:15 PM CST Tuesday the stage was 6.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.7 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 5.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Western Arctic Coast; Northwest Arctic Coast; Northern Arctic Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow. Additional snow accumulations of 1 to
3 inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Northern and Western Arctic Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Snow and blowing snow could
reduce visibility below one half mile at times. Blizzard conditions
will be intermittently possible, especially in Utqiagvik.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of blowing snow may persist into the
weekend as gusty wind and areas of falling snow continue at times.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Blizzard conditions. Additional snow accumulations up to two
inches. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph.

* WHERE...Central Beaufort Sea Coast and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be impacted. Areas of blowing snow could
significantly reduce visibility below 1/4 mile due to falling and
blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Periods of light snow and wind will persist
into the weekend. The snow will become a bit more intermittent
tonight into tomorrow but with strong east winds, blizzard
conditions may continue longer than currently expected. Regardless
of blizzard conditions, periods of blowing snow will persist into
the weekend. We will continue to monitor and update as necessary.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton; Cascade County below 5000ft
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Gusty westerly winds are producing periods of localized reduced
visibility, particularly along the Interstate 15 corridor. If you
will be traveling on Interstate 15 this afternoon, be prepared for
areas of reduced visibility to around a mile or so. If you encounter
blowing dust, make sure that your headlights are on so you are more
visible to others on the roadways.
